title: unfirehose/1.0 Throttle
description: A provider refused a call. Its own record type rather than a field on a message, because a throttled call usually produces no message at all — the request failed before any content existed to attach it to. Harnesses that route across several providers MUST set `upstream`: 'we were rate limited' is not actionable when the remedy depends on which of five providers said no.

sessionId.description: Session the refused call belonged to

kind.description: How the provider refused, because each calls for a different response. The four throttle kinds: rate_limit — too many requests per unit time, slow down or spread load. concurrency — too many calls in flight, queue them; retrying harder makes it worse. quota — plan or credit exhausted, waiting does not help until it resets. overloaded — the provider ran out of capacity, not caused by our usage. The four non-throttle refusals, added in 1.0.1 because a harness that only records throttles loses the rest: model_gone — 404/410, this host no longer serves that model, so route elsewhere rather than retry (a deregistered model looks exactly like a working one until it 404s). server_error — 5xx from the provider. timeout — no answer within the deadline. content_policy — a safety filter refused. A refusal caused by OUR request (a malformed body, a bad key, an oversized prompt) is NOT a throttle record: the remedy is the payload, and recording it here reports provider trouble that never happened.

upstream.description: The provider that actually refused — 'openrouter', 'nous', 'anthropic', 'x-ai', or a self-hosted endpoint key. The single most valuable field here. A harness that omits it records that it was throttled but not by whom, which cannot be recovered downstream: the endpoint is not in the message, and inferring from the session's model is wrong whenever the failing call used a different one (a vision call does not use the chat model).

endpoint.description: Full URL of the API that refused. Lets a self-hosted throttle be attributed to a specific box.

model.description: Model being requested when refused. MUST be the model of the failing call, not the session default.

operation.description: Which call was refused — 'chat', 'vision', 'embed', 'rerank'. Narrows the fix even when `upstream` is unknown: a throttled vision endpoint points at the vision model, not the chat model.

retryAfterSeconds.description: What the provider asked us to wait, from the Retry-After header or an equivalent field. Recording it lets backoff follow what was actually requested instead of a guess.

attempts.description: How many attempts were made before giving up. One event per failed call, not one per attempt — counting retries as separate throttles overstates how often a provider refused.

recovered.description: True when a later attempt or a failover succeeded. Distinguishes a throttle we absorbed from one that cost the user a turn.

failoverTo.description: Upstream we fell back to, when the harness rerouted. Makes routing pressure visible: repeated failover away from one provider is a signal about that provider.

message.description: Provider's error text, verbatim and untruncated where practical.
